- Human answer: Accepted recommended default

## Process revision — bulk-draft-then-veto for [Standard] terms
- Date: 2026-09-22
- Context: initial 11-term pass was flagged as too thin for an org-wide
  Infrastructure domain. Human asked why standard-sourced definitions
  weren't just bulk-loaded with source citations instead of one-by-one Q&A.
- Resolution: two-bucket model adopted going forward for all domains —
  [Standard] terms (objective, standards-sourced, no judgment call) are
  bulk-drafted and presented as one table for scan-and-veto; [Org-decision]
  terms (standard leaves it open, or a real org-specific choice) stay in
  the one-by-one Q&A pattern.
- Applies to: all domains, all future Definitions/Taxonomy passes.

## Q1.7 — Scope: do AI-specific compute terms belong in Infrastructure?
- Type: Judgment (scoping) · Required · Human-only
- Options presented: Keep in Infrastructure / Move to System Architecture /
  Move to Harness
- AI recommendation: Keep in Infrastructure (closest to the hardware they
  describe)
- Human answer: raised a structural question first (see Q1.8) before
  answering directly — resolution below implies "keep in Infrastructure,
  tagged Referenced By other domains" was accepted as the working answer
- Decision-weight: Medium
- Resulting term(s): Inference Workload, Training Workload, GPU Memory
  (VRAM), Model-Serving Node — all owned by Infrastructure
- Date answered: 2026-09-22

## Q1.8 — Cross-domain term linking mechanism (DRY / anti-drift)
- Type: Judgment (structural/process) · Required · Human-raised
- Human question: how do we cite which domain(s) a definition is associated
  with, and how do we avoid duplicating/drifting definitions across domains?
- Resolution: single-owner-per-term rule. Term defined once, in its owner
  domain's Definitions file, under an anchored heading
  (`### Term {#domain-prefix-term-slug}`). Other domains reference it via a
  markdown link, never a redefinition. Owner entry carries a
  "Referenced by:" line for the reverse direction. Unified glossary
  (00-framework/glossary-master.md) generated by scanning anchors across
  all domains — links only, no copied text.
- Full rule recorded in: 00-framework/term-linking-convention.md
- Decision-weight: High (governs all future domains, not just this one)
- Date answered: 2026-09-22
